verdict.rationale: Cognee documents a multi-user permissions system with dataset-scoped permissions and per-dataset storage, so multiple users or organizations can share one instance while their data stays completely separate. Sessions are also keyed by (user_id, session_id), and the founder describes per-user graphs combined with user permissions and graph filtering. missing for 10: explicit per-agent memory scoping, detailed docs on how recall enforces isolation across tenants, independent or hands-on corroboration of no cross-tenant leakage.

support.subject: As a developer, I can scope memories per user, agent, or application so one tenant's memories never leak into another's retrieval

citations.quote: This system provides data isolation and access control through dataset-scoped permissions and per-dataset storage, enabling multiple users or organizations to use the same Cognee instance while keeping their data completely separate.
A session is Cognee's short-term memory for a specific user. It is identified by `(user_id, session_id)`
we have graphs per user now available. So, user permissions + graph filtering.
